payments.title: Shopify Payments & payouts
payments.summary: Shopify Payments (or a third-party gateway) authorizes cards at checkout, then later transfers settled funds to your bank. A hold, test-mode flag, or missing provider blocks money — not always checkout.
payments.why_this_ui: Banners on Home and Settings → Payments are written by Risk / Payments, not by your theme. Staff accounts often cannot see the same hold details as the store owner.

shipping.title: Shipping profiles, zones & rates
shipping.summary: Checkout asks every matching shipping profile for a rate. If the country is missing, a carrier API returns nothing, or the product has no weight, the customer sees “no shipping methods”.
shipping.why_this_ui: The empty-rate banner is a checkout result, not a payments error. Draft-order tests with the customer’s city and postal code are the fastest way to reproduce it.

themes.title: Online Store themes & Liquid
themes.summary: Themes render your storefront. A Liquid syntax error, missing snippet, or broken app embed can take down a section — or the whole preview — without touching orders.
themes.why_this_ui: “Theme has errors” is a compile-time check. Duplicate the theme before editing. App embeds often look like theme bugs.

apps.title: Apps, embeds & checkout extensions
apps.summary: Apps inject scripts, theme embeds, and checkout UI extensions. After a theme switch or app update they can override buttons, hide rates, or break save.
apps.why_this_ui: Shopify rarely names the offending app in the banner. The cleanest test is: unpublished theme preview → disable embeds one by one → retest.

inventory.title: Inventory, locations & overselling
inventory.summary: Available stock is on-hand minus committed, per location. Oversell, missing location, or “continue selling when out of stock” off will block checkout or fulfillment.
inventory.why_this_ui: Red “insufficient inventory” toasts fire when a fulfill or cart change asks a location that has no available units.

permissions.title: Staff permissions & store owner
permissions.summary: Many Payments, billing, and legal banners are owner-only. A staff user can see a red banner and still lack the button that clears it.
permissions.why_this_ui: “You don’t have permission” toasts are not store bugs. Retry as the store owner or grant the Finance / Settings permission.

domains.title: Domains, DNS & SSL
domains.summary: Shopify looks for a specific A/CNAME pair. Extra AAAA or old records stall verification and SSL.
domains.why_this_ui: Domain banners live under Online Store → Domains. Checkout on a custom domain fails until Connected + primary + SSL issued.

checkout.title: Checkout, Shop Pay & 3-D Secure
checkout.summary: Checkout combines rates, taxes, markets, and the payment provider. 3-D Secure, Shop Pay, and wallets add an extra bank challenge that can fail independently of your gateway.
checkout.why_this_ui: Order timeline lists the exact decline code. Admin toasts after Capture/Refund are provider responses, not theme errors.

billing.title: Shopify billing & subscriptions
billing.summary: Your Shopify invoice (plan + apps) is separate from customer payouts. A failed Shopify bill can lock features or show a store-wide banner.
billing.why_this_ui: Past-due banners sit at the top of every admin page. Fix them under Settings → Billing, not Payments.

general.title: Admin, notifications & markets
general.summary: Anything that is not payments, shipping, or the theme — taxes, pixels, gift cards, markets, email auth — still writes banners in the same Polaris chrome.
general.why_this_ui: Read the banner first. The page title is often broader than the actual blocker.
